correctness.rationale: Let P be the announcement upset and Q the truth upset of B on the restriction, viewed in the original frame; Q remains upward closed since P is an upset. At s in P, write T=R[up(s)]. Using the stated future-world necessity, the left side tests T intersect P contained in Q, while the right tests up(T) intersect P contained in Q. Outside P each evaluation is the corresponding test over future s in P. Thus frame validity is equivalent to up(T intersect P)=up(T) intersect P for all s in P and all upsets P: necessity can already be tested with atoms p=P and q=up(T intersect P), and equality suffices for any formulas. For w in up(T) intersect P choose v>=s and vRu<=w; AR gives v'>=v and u'<=w with v'Ru' and u' above v or w. This puts u' in T intersect P. Conversely if AR fails at vRu<=w, set s=v and P=up(v) union up(w); then w lies in up(T) intersect P, but not in up(T intersect P) by absence of the AR witness. This yields the atomic countervaluation and proves all-cardinalities equivalence, including nonantisymmetric preorders and the empty announcement upset. Forward confluence witnesses AR by u'=w. On 0<1 the sole arrow 0R0 satisfies AR but violates forward confluence; the sole arrow 1R0 fails AR with p={1}, q empty. Reflexivity rules out a one-world counterexample. Independently evaluating restriction, box and implication with bitset operations (python /workspace/review-work/check-announcement.py) reproduced the all-labelled-preorder triples (1,2,2), (4,64,56), (29,14848,9571), and the fixed-chain pairs of valid and strictly nonconfluent valid counts (12,1), (224,26), (14592,1215). The finite census does not prove the unrestricted correspondence.

value.rationale: This pinpoints exactly when a named reduction remains sound after removing structural hypotheses, rather than just giving a counterexample. The equivalence with a single atomic test and the strict two-world separation make the condition usable for frame analysis and distinguish it from forward confluence. The result is an all-cardinalities correspondence, not merely a finite enumeration or a claim about full eliminability.
